newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan court rejects Red Army appeal in 1970s hijack.
newsitem.headline: Japan court rejects Red Army appeal in 1970s hijack.

text.p: A Japanese appeals court on Tuesday upheld a lower court decision to sentence a key member of the Japanese Red Army to life imprisonment for masterminding two hijackings in the 1970s.

Presiding Judge Mitsuru Kobayashi of the Tokyo High Court rejected Osamu Maruoka's appeal against a life sentence handed down by a lower court in 1993, saying he was responsible for "extremely dangerous and vicious crimes".
Judge Kobayashi said Maruoka, 46, was guilty of masterminding two hijackings of Japan Airlines (JAL) planes in the 1970s.
It was not clear if Maruoka will appeal Tuesday's ruling to the Supreme Court.

In 1973, Maruoka's group hijacked a JAL plane bound for Tokyo from Paris and forced it to land at Dubai, in the United Arab Emirates. After releasing the hostages, the group blew up the plane in Libya.
In 1977, Maruoka led a five-member Japanese Red Army group in the hijacking of a JAL flight to Dhaka, Bangladesh.
The group won the release of six convicted colleagues from Japanese jails and $6 million cash in ransom from the Japanese government in exchange for hostages.
At the time, Japan came under severe international criticism for releasing the convicts and paying the ransom.
Maruoka was arrested a decade after the second hijacking in December 1987 in Tokyo after secretly returning to Japan from a Japanese Red Army hideout in Lebanon, using a forged passport.
About 20 members of the ageing Japanese Red Army, led by female leader Fusako Shigenobu, 51, run a guerrilla training camp in Lebanon's Bekaa valley, Japanese police say.
In February, five Japanese Red Army members were arrested in Beirut and charged with using false passports. Japan sought their extradition but Lebanon decided to put them on trial.
